# Behavioral Specification: ENTROPY_SRC Core

## 1. Overview

The ENTROPY_SRC core is the digital processing heart of the entropy source IP. It collects raw entropy samples from an external physical noise source, applies statistical health tests, optionally conditions the entropy using a SHA3-based conditioner, and makes full-entropy seeds available either to a hardware consumer or to firmware through a register interface.

The core operates in two broad entropy-delivery modes:

- **Normal / FIPS-compliant mode**: raw entropy is health tested, conditioned by SHA3, and delivered with a FIPS-compliant indicator.
- **Bypass / boot-time mode**: raw entropy is health tested with bypass-mode thresholds, skips the conditioner, and is packed directly into seeds. This mode provides lower-latency entropy during boot and is not FIPS-compliant.

Firmware override mode is also supported. In this mode, raw entropy can be observed by firmware, and firmware-written data can be inserted into the conditioning path.

## 2. Interfaces

The core has the following externally observable interfaces:

- Clock and reset.
- A configuration/status register interface used by firmware to control the core and observe status.
- A raw entropy source interface that supplies 4-bit entropy samples and a valid indication.
- An entropy consumer interface that uses a request/acknowledge handshake to receive 384-bit entropy seeds and a FIPS-compliance flag.
- A halt request/acknowledge interface used to coordinate activity with the AES/CSRNG logic.
- An external health test interface that provides raw entropy and control signals to a vendor-specific health test block and receives test results back.
- Recoverable alert and fatal alert outputs, plus alert test outputs.
- Four interrupt outputs: entropy available, health test failed, observe FIFO ready, and fatal error.

## 3. Reset, Enable, and Disable

### 3.1 Reset behavior

After reset, the core shall be in the disabled state. All internal FIFOs, counters, health-test state, and status state shall be cleared. No entropy shall be collected, no RNG enable shall be asserted, and alert and interrupt outputs shall be deasserted.

The core shall re-arm bypass/boot-time mode during reset. Therefore, the first enable after reset causes the core to operate in bypass mode unless boot-time bypass is explicitly disabled by configuration or fuse state.

### 3.2 Enable behavior

The core shall enter the enabled state only when the enable configuration field has the defined True encoding.

- If the enable field is not defined as True, the core shall not enable entropy collection.
- If the enable field has an invalid encoding, the core shall remain disabled and shall assert a recoverable alert and set a corresponding status bit.

The enabled state is registered. A write to the enable field shall take effect on the following clock edge.

When enabled, the core shall:

- Assert the RNG enable output.
- Accept raw entropy samples from the noise source.
- Run health tests on the incoming entropy stream.
- Begin producing and delivering entropy seeds.

### 3.3 Disable behavior

When the core is disabled:

- The RNG enable output shall be deasserted.
- No new entropy samples shall be accepted.
- Internal data path FIFOs shall be cleared.
- Health-test counters and status counters shall return to their reset state.
- Bypass/boot-time mode shall be re-armed, so a subsequent enable again starts in bypass mode unless it is explicitly disabled.

## 4. Raw Entropy Collection

When enabled, the core shall accept 4-bit raw entropy samples from the external noise source.

The core shall provide flow control to the noise source by asserting the RNG enable output only when enabled. Raw samples are consumed only when the core is enabled and the source indicates that valid data is present.

### 4.1 Bit-serial sampling mode

The core supports an optional bit-serial sampling mode. When this mode is enabled:

- The core shall select one bit from each 4-bit raw sample, based on the programmed bit-selection value.
- The selected bits shall be packed into 4-bit symbols before being sent to the health tests.
- Entropy produced while bit-serial mode is enabled shall not be marked FIPS-compliant.

When bit-serial mode is disabled, the full 4-bit raw sample shall be used directly as the health-test symbol.

## 5. Health Testing

Health testing shall be active whenever the core is enabled. The raw entropy symbol stream is presented to all enabled health tests.

The following health tests shall be performed:

- **Repetition Count Test**: detects an excessive number of consecutive equal symbols. This test is continuous and shall not reset at window boundaries.
- **Repetition Count Symbol Test**: detects an excessive concentration of the same symbol in the observed stream.
- **Adaptive Proportion Test**: detects bias in the number of ones over a window, using high and low thresholds.
- **Bucket Test**: detects bias in the frequency distribution of 4-bit symbols over a window.
- **Markov Test**: detects unexpected first-order temporal correlations in the bit stream.
- **External Health Test**: provides the same entropy stream to an external vendor-specific test block and accepts external pass/fail results.

### 5.1 Health-test windowing

The core shall maintain a window counter for health testing. Each valid raw entropy symbol increments the window counter.

The window length shall be selected based on the current mode:

- In normal FIPS mode, the FIPS health-test window shall be used.
- In bypass/boot-time mode, the bypass health-test window shall be used.

When the window counter reaches the programmed window length, the core shall generate a window-done event and reset the window counter.

Window-based tests shall evaluate pass/fail at each window-done event. The repetition count test shall not be reset by the window boundary.

### 5.2 Thresholds

Each health test shall have separate threshold values for FIPS mode and bypass mode. The threshold set used by the test shall be selected according to the current mode.

Threshold registers are one-way. After a threshold has been programmed, subsequent writes shall only be able to move the active threshold in the more restrictive direction. This prevents accidental or malicious weakening of health-test limits without a reset or clear.

### 5.3 Health-test clear

Firmware can request a health-test clear. When this clear is asserted:

- The window counter shall be reset.
- All health-test counters shall be cleared.
- All watermarks and fail counters shall be cleared.
- The external health-test clear output shall be asserted so that external test logic is also reset.

### 5.4 Health-test results and failure handling

Whenever any individual health test detects a failure, the core shall:

- Increment the corresponding total fail counter.
- Increment the summary fail counter.
- Update the relevant fail counters used for alert generation.
- Set a pending health-test-failed condition.

If a health-test failure is pending, newly generated entropy seeds shall not be written to the final entropy FIFO. The pending failure shall remain set until the next health-test window-done event occurs or until the core is disabled or cleared.

The core shall also track high and low watermarks for the statistics measured by each health test, separately for FIPS and bypass modes. These values shall be exposed to firmware for diagnostic purposes.

## 6. Entropy Conditioning and Bypass

After health testing, raw entropy symbols shall be packed into wider words for the conditioning stage.

### 6.1 Normal mode

In normal mode, the packed raw entropy shall be fed into the SHA3-based conditioner.

The conditioner shall:

- Operate in SHA3 mode with a 384-bit output width.
- Accept data only when its input is ready.
- Produce a 384-bit conditioned value when enough entropy has been absorbed.

The core shall not feed data into the conditioner while a halt request to the AES/CSRNG logic is outstanding. The conditioner may only proceed after the halt request has been acknowledged.

### 6.2 Bypass mode

In bypass mode, the SHA3 conditioner shall not be used. Instead, the packed raw entropy shall be packed directly into 384-bit seeds.

Bypass mode shall be selected under the following conditions:

- The core is in boot-time mode after reset, unless boot-time bypass has been disabled.
- Firmware or configuration explicitly selects the bypass path.
- The main state machine requests a return to bypass mode, for example after completing a boot-time seed.

### 6.3 Final seed generation

The core shall generate 384-bit entropy seeds from either the conditioned path or the bypass path.

A seed shall be written to the final entropy FIFO only if:

- The final FIFO is not full.
- No health-test failure is currently pending.
- The transfer is authorized by the main control state machine.

## 7. Entropy Storage and Delivery

### 7.1 Final entropy FIFO

The core shall maintain a final entropy FIFO for completed 384-bit seeds. Each FIFO entry shall also carry a one-bit FIPS-compliant indicator.

The FIPS-compliant indicator shall be asserted only when:

- The core is enabled.
- The seed was produced in normal mode, not bypass mode.
- Full-width raw RNG samples were used, not bit-serial sampling.

### 7.2 Hardware entropy delivery

When hardware delivery is selected, the core shall present seeds to the hardware entropy consumer through a request/acknowledge handshake.

The core shall:

- Not acknowledge a hardware request unless a seed is available in the final FIFO.
- Present the 384-bit seed and the FIPS-compliant indicator to the consumer when the handshake completes.
- Pop the final FIFO only when the consumer acknowledges and a seed is successfully transferred.

If no seed is available, the core shall hold the hardware request until a seed becomes available.

### 7.3 Software entropy delivery

When software delivery is selected, seeds from the final FIFO shall be routed into a software unpacking FIFO instead of being sent to the hardware interface.

The software unpacking FIFO shall make the seed available as 32-bit words through the entropy data register. A 384-bit seed requires twelve 32-bit reads to be fully consumed.

The entropy-available interrupt shall be asserted whenever the software unpacking FIFO contains data that can be read.

Reads from the entropy data register shall pop data from the software unpacking FIFO only when all of the following are true:

- The core is enabled.
- The fuse setting allows software entropy register reads.
- The entropy data register enable configuration field is True.

Otherwise, reads shall return zero and shall not consume entropy data.

## 8. Firmware Override and Observe Mode

The core supports a firmware override mode. This mode shall be active only when both:

- The fuse override enable input is asserted.
- The firmware override mode configuration field is set to the defined True value.

When firmware override mode is active:

- Post-health-test entropy words shall be captured into an observe FIFO.
- The core shall assert the observe-FIFO-ready interrupt when the observe FIFO depth reaches the programmed threshold.
- Firmware can read words from the observe FIFO through the register interface.

To prevent the observe FIFO from overflowing, the core shall discard the oldest entry when the FIFO is full and a new entry arrives.

Firmware override mode also allows firmware-written data to be inserted into the entropy pipeline:

- When firmware insert mode is enabled, firmware write data shall be accepted into the pre-conditioning path.
- When firmware insert mode is disabled, the normal post-health-test stream shall continue to flow into the pre-conditioning path.

Health testing remains active in firmware override mode.

## 9. External Health Test Interface

The core shall provide an external health test interface so that a vendor-specific test block can observe and test the same entropy stream used by the internal tests.

The core shall output to the external health test block:

- The raw entropy symbol stream.
- A valid indication for each symbol.
- An active indication, asserted when the core is enabled.
- A clear indication, asserted on health-test clear.
- The currently selected high and low thresholds.
- The currently selected health-test window size.

The core shall accept from the external health test block:

- A measured test count.
- A high-threshold failure pulse.
- A low-threshold failure pulse.

External health-test failure pulses shall be treated like internal failures. They shall increment the external health-test fail counters and contribute to the summary health-test failure and alert status.

## 10. Halt Coordination

Before using the SHA3 conditioner, the core shall request a halt from the AES/CSRNG logic. The core shall wait for the halt to be acknowledged before feeding data to the conditioner.

The halt request shall be asserted only while coordination is required and shall be deasserted after the conditioning operation has completed.

## 11. Alerts

### 11.1 Recoverable alert

The recoverable alert output shall be asserted whenever any recoverable alert condition is present. Recoverable alert conditions include:

- An invalid encoding in any multi-bit secure configuration field.
- A health-test alert threshold being reached.
- A main control state-machine alert condition.
- Detection of repeated consecutive entropy data values by the data-integrity monitor.

The recoverable alert output is level-based and reflects the presence of an active recoverable condition.

### 11.2 Fatal alert

The fatal alert output shall be asserted when a fatal internal error is detected. Fatal error conditions include:

- Internal FIFO write errors, such as a write to a full FIFO.
- Internal FIFO read errors, such as a read from an empty FIFO.
- Internal FIFO state errors, such as a full but empty FIFO.
- Entropy acknowledge state-machine errors.
- Main state-machine errors.
- Counter errors detected by duplicated counter logic.

Counter errors shall be reported even when the core is disabled. Other fatal errors shall be reported when the core is enabled.

### 11.3 Alert test outputs

The alert test inputs shall cause a corresponding pulse on the recoverable or fatal alert test output. Alert test pulses shall not change the normal alert status registers.

## 12. Interrupts

The core shall provide four interrupt outputs.

### 12.1 Entropy available interrupt

This interrupt shall be asserted when the software unpacking FIFO contains entropy data that firmware can read. This indicates that entropy is ready to be consumed through the entropy data register.

### 12.2 Health-test-failed interrupt

This interrupt shall be asserted when a health-test failure is escalated by the main control state machine, such as when the health-test alert threshold has been reached. It indicates that the health tests have detected a statistically significant problem with the raw entropy stream.

### 12.3 Observe-FIFO-ready interrupt

This interrupt shall be asserted when firmware override mode is active and the observe FIFO depth meets or exceeds the programmed threshold. It indicates that firmware can read raw observed entropy.

### 12.4 Fatal-error interrupt

This interrupt shall be asserted when a fatal internal error condition is detected and the interrupt is enabled.

Each interrupt output shall be controlled by the corresponding interrupt enable, interrupt state, and interrupt test registers. An event shall set the interrupt state, and the interrupt output shall be asserted only when the interrupt state is set and enabled.

## 13. Error Reporting

The core shall report fatal error conditions in status registers. Error status bits shall be set when the corresponding error condition is detected and shall remain set until cleared by software.

The following error categories shall be reported:

- Raw entropy input FIFO errors.
- Observe FIFO errors.
- Final entropy FIFO errors.
- Entropy acknowledge state-machine errors.
- Main state-machine errors.
- Counter errors.
- Composite FIFO write errors.
- Composite FIFO read errors.
- Composite FIFO state errors.

When an error status bit is set, the corresponding error status field shall be reflected to firmware through the register interface.

## 14. Data Integrity Monitoring

The core shall monitor the final entropy output stream for repeated data patterns.

If two consecutive 64-bit portions of the final entropy output match, the core shall treat this as a potential entropy source malfunction and assert a recoverable alert.

This data-integrity check shall be active when the core is enabled and shall be cleared when the core is disabled.

## 15. Summary of Operational Modes

| Mode | Conditioning | Health-test window | FIPS flag | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Normal FIPS mode | SHA3 conditioner used | FIPS window | Asserted | Full-entropy seeds for CSRNG and firmware |
| Bypass/boot-time mode | SHA3 skipped | Bypass window | Deasserted | Low-latency initial entropy |
| Firmware override mode | Raw entropy observable; optional firmware insertion | Same window selection | Depends on selected path | Custom firmware health tests or conditioning |

The core shall automatically select the correct thresholds, window size, conditioning path, and FIPS indication based on the current mode and configuration.
